name: Al-Mansur Founds Baghdad, Abbasid Golden City
summary: Caliph al-Mansur founds the 'City of Peace' (Madinat al-Salam) at Baghdad in 762, a perfectly circular planned city with four gates aligned to the cardinal directions. Within a generation it is the world's largest city (population estimates range from 500,000 to 1,000,000). The Round City's design, palace and mosque at the center, administrative districts in concentric rings, is a physical embodiment of Abbasid claims to universal caliphate.

_quarry.structural_significance: Baghdad's foundation moves the center of the Islamic world from Syria (Umayyad Damascus) to Iraq (near ancient Babylon and Ctesiphon), signaling the Abbasid break from Arab tribalism toward Persian-influenced cosmopolitan empire; the city's size and wealth make it the most important cultural center of the medieval world for 300 years; its destruction by the Mongols (1258) is the single greatest cultural catastrophe of the medieval period
